column1: # Who a new issue belongs to, per repository. One definition for every repo on the board.
# Columns: repo <TAB> login
# A COLUMN IS THE BYTES BETWEEN THE TABS. A row carries EXACTLY ONE TAB, and neither column may
# begin or end with a SPACE. Both readers refuse anything else and name the row; neither trims,
# because a reader that repairs a file decides for you what you meant. A comment opens with `#`
# in column one, and a blank line is empty - an indented one is neither and is refused.
# An issue lands on whoever OWNS that repository, not on whoever happened to type the
# command. Without this file, every issue is created with `@me` and then corrected by
# hand - which works exactly as long as nobody forgets, and somebody always does.
# The login is the GitHub ACCOUNT NAME, the one the API accepts, never the display name.
# A repo that is not listed falls back to `@me`. That is deliberate: a new repo should
# assign to the person setting it up rather than fail, and adding a line here is how it
# stops doing that. An explicit --assignee / -Assignee always wins over both.
# Adding an owner means adding a line here, never passing the login by hand each time.
# THE MAP IS EMPTY ON PURPOSE. Who owns which repository is not known in advance, and a
# guessed owner is worse than none: it assigns work to somebody who never agreed to it
# and hides that the question was never asked. Until a repository has an agreed owner,
# `@me` is the correct answer. Add a line the moment one is agreed - one line per repo,
# in the form below.
# example-org/example-repo
